ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the temporal bone

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral hearing loss with aural fullness and otorrhea
salient_findings: Polypoid mass in the right external auditory canal
Right profound sensorineural hearing loss on pure-tone audiometry
key_facts: 4-year history of right aural fullness
Initial right middle ear effusion
No improvement with intranasal steroids and antihistamines
Myringotomy with insertion of a pressure-equalizing tube was performed
Painless right otorrhea developed 4 months prior to evaluation
Sensation that the right ear was shallower than the left
Polypoid mass occluded the right external auditory canal
Purulent discharge in the right external auditory canal
Right tympanic membrane was not visualized
Left ear and facial nerve function were normal
High-resolution CT showed an irregularly enhancing mass in the right ear canal, middle ear cavity, and mastoid air cells

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the temporal bone
shortlist.why_kept: Irregularly enhancing mass and progressive hearing loss suggest a malignant process

shortlist.label: Aggressive papillary middle ear tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive features and location in the middle ear cavity are consistent with this rare tumor

shortlist.label: Ceruminous adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location in the ear canal and presence of a polypoid mass are consistent with ceruminous adenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Malignant otitis externa
shortlist.why_kept: Painless otorrhea and presence of a polypoid mass are consistent with malignant otitis externa

raw.rationale: The patient's history of chronic ear symptoms, including aural fullness and otorrhea, along with the presence of a polypoid mass and erosive changes of the skull base on CT, are consistent with a cholesteatoma. The lack of pain and the gradual progression of symptoms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the temporal bone
rejected.why: While possible, this diagnosis is less likely due to the patient's age and the absence of other symptoms such as facial weakness or pain.

rejected.label: Aggressive papillary middle ear tumor
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the lack of specific symptoms and imaging findings characteristic of this rare tumor.

rejected.label: Ceruminous adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is unlikely as it typically presents with a mass in the external auditory canal and is often associated with pain and other symptoms not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Malignant otitis externa
rejected.why: This diagnosis is unlikely as it typically presents with severe pain and is often associated with diabetes or immunocompromised states, which are not mentioned in the vignette.
